sections.name: problem_summary
sections.content: The fictional department needs a more consistent intake process and a preliminary improvement plan.

sections.name: findings
sections.content: The fixture establishes a six-week horizon and asks for a structured improvement deliverable.

sections.name: alternatives
sections.content: Alternative A standardizes intake with a checklist. Alternative B adds a triage step before assignment.

sections.name: recommendation
sections.content: Pilot a standardized intake checklist first, then add triage if the pilot shows unresolved routing delays.

sections.name: implementation_steps
sections.content: Week 1 map the process; Week 2 draft the checklist; Weeks 3-4 pilot; Week 5 measure results; Week 6 revise and document.

sections.name: risks
sections.content: Risks include low adoption, unclear ownership, and overfitting the process to the synthetic fixture.

sections.name: assumptions
sections.content: This demonstration assumes the fictional department can run a six-week pilot and that no restricted data is required.

sections.name: missing_information
sections.content: Real staffing levels, baseline processing times, and budget evidence are not provided by the fixture.

sections.name: sources
sections.content: Two controlled synthetic fixture passages are used for this Week 1 demonstration.

sections.name: expert_review_needs
sections.content: A City process owner should verify feasibility, staffing assumptions, and any operational changes before use.
